# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👆 👇]

I'm the Deaf monkey. I see the bomb: display reads 0, light is orange, and there are three wires — red (1), yellow (2), blue (3).

I can't hear anything, but I received two gestures this round. Let me think about who sent what and what reaches them.

The speaking order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. So this round, Mute and Blind both acted before me. Their messages land on whoever comes after them in that same round.

- Mute gestures: Mute can only gesture to... wait. Mute's gestures: who can see gestures? Deaf and Mute can see (Blind cannot see). But the note says "Mute gestures to Deaf" — so Mute directed it to me. I receive gestures. Good.
- Blind gestures: Blind can gesture, and gestures are seen by whoever can see. I'm Deaf — I can see. So Blind's gesture reached me too.

Now, what do these gestures mean? Nobody has established a code yet. The gestures are just symbols. I see:
- From Mute: [👆 🤟] — pointing up, and "I love you" / love-you sign.
- From Blind: [✋ 👆 👇] — open hand, point up, point down.

These are raw symbols with no agreed meaning. I need to establish meaning. But I also need to share what I see, because I'm the only one who can see the bomb.

Key insight: Blind can touch the bomb but can't see it. Mute can read the manual but can't speak or touch. I can see but can't touch or hear. We need to connect.

What do I know? Display 0, light orange, wires red/yellow/blue. The manual (Mute) presumably tells what to do given certain conditions. Blind can feel the bomb — maybe wire positions, maybe the display, maybe the light.

I should describe the bomb to the others. I speak — Mute and Blind receive my speech. Wait: when I speak, Mute and Blind receive it. Blind can hear! Blind cannot see, but can hear. Mute can hear too (Mute just can't speak). So my speech reaches both Mute and Blind. Good — that's my main channel.

When I gesture, only Mute receives it (Blind can't see). So gestures are less useful for broadcasting.

So I should SPEAK to describe the bomb. Let me describe: display shows 0, light is orange, wires numbered 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

I should also try to establish what the gestures meant. But since no code is set, I'll ask. Actually, I can't hear their speech, so I only got gestures. I should tell them what I saw as gestures and ask them to clarify — but I can only speak (to Mute and Blind) and gesture (to Mute).

Let me think about what's most useful. The critical thing: I see the bomb. I must convey: display=0, light=orange, wires red/yellow/blue in positions 1/2/3.

Let me send that clearly. I'll speak to both (unnamed reaches everyone who can hear = Mute and Blind).

Also I might gesture to Mute to acknowledge, but let's keep it focused. I'll describe the bomb and note I received gestures but don't know their meaning yet.

Let me write the calls.

I'll speak: "I see the bomb. Display reads 0. Light is orange. Three wires: position 1 red, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue. I received gestures from both of you but no code is agreed — please tell me what they mean. I cannot hear speech, so send me gestures or have Mute relay."

Wait — can Blind send me gestures? Blind gestures, I can see. Yes. And Mute gestures, I can see. So both can gesture to me. Good.

But Blind can't see my gestures. And Mute can hear my speech and see my gestures. Blind can hear my speech.

So to reach Blind: speech only. To reach Mute: speech or gesture.

Let me send speech to everyone (Mute + Blind) describing the bomb.

I'll also gesture to Mute maybe to confirm receipt. But keep it minimal and clear.

Let me produce the calls.I'm the Deaf monkey, and I'm the only one who can see the bomb. This round I received two gestures (from Mute and from Blind), but no code has been agreed, so they're just raw symbols to me — I can't assume meaning. My job is to broadcast what I see, since I'm the sole source of visual information.

Key channel facts: when I speak, both Mute and Blind hear me (Blind can hear, just not see). When I gesture, only Mute sees it. So speech is my broadcast channel; gestures reach only Mute.

I'll describe the bomb fully and ask for the gestures to be explained, and I'll gesture a simple acknowledgment to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see the bomb. Display reads 0. Light is orange. Three wires: position 1 is red, position 2 is yellow, position 3 is blue. I received gestures from both of you but no code is agreed, so I do not know what they mean. I cannot hear speech. Please send me gestures, or have Mute relay the manual to me by gesture.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see the bomb. Display reads 0. Light is orange. Three wires: position 1 is red, position 2 is yellow, position 3 is blue. I received your gesture but no code is agreed, so I do not know what it means. I cannot hear speech and you cannot see my gestures, so we must connect through Mute.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

Wait, that's crucial. Mute can only gesture (seen by Deaf, and by Mute? no). Mute's gestures are seen by whoever can see: Deaf and... Blind can't see. So Mute's gestures reach only Deaf. Mute's speech: none. So Mute can ONLY communicate to Deaf.

Blind can speak (heard by Mute and Deaf-hearers... I can't hear). Blind can touch. Blind's speech reaches Mute. Blind's gestures reach Deaf (and Mute? Mute can see). So Blind→Mute via speech, Blind→Deaf via gesture.

Deaf (me): speech reaches Mute and Blind. Gesture reaches Mute only.

So the graph:
- Mute → Deaf (gesture only)
- Blind → Mute (speech), Blind → Deaf (gesture)
- Deaf → Mute (speech+gesture), Deaf → Blind (speech)

The manual is with Mute. Mute can only tell Deaf (via gesture). Deaf can then tell Blind (via speech). So the manual's rule must flow: Mute → Deaf → Blind. And I'm the relay!

That's the key realization. I am the bridge between Mute (manual) and Blind (hands). Mute tells me the rule by gesture; I relay it to Blind by speech.

So I must get the rule from Mute via gesture and relay to Blind. Let me explicitly set this up.

I'll speak to Blind: "Mute holds the manual but can only gesture to me. I will relay the rule to you. Tell me what you can feel on the bomb." And gesture to Mute: "send me the rule."

Let me do that.Critical realization about the communication graph:

- Mute can only gesture, and gestures are seen only by those who can see — that's me (Deaf) and Mute. Blind cannot see gestures. Mute cannot speak. So **Mute can only ever communicate with me.**
- Blind can speak (heard by Mute) and gesture (seen by me).
- I can speak (heard by Mute and Blind) and gesture (seen by Mute).

So the manual sits with Mute, who can only reach me by gesture. Blind has the hands but can't see. **I am the only bridge: Mute → me (gesture) → Blind (speech).** I must set this relay up explicitly.

Light is now red (orange → green → red over three rounds). Display 0, wires unchanged.

The light has cycled orange, then green, then red across the rounds.")
```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, you can only reach me by gesture, and I am the only one who can relay your manual to Blind by speech. Send me the rule from the manual as gestures, symbol by symbol, and I will speak it to Blind. Tell me: what does the manual say to do given the light colour and the display?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "👆", "👉", "✌", "👌"])
```
